title: Article 87 — Special address by the President

content.overview: Article 87 requires the President to address both Houses of Parliament assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election to the House of the People and at the commencement of the first session of each year, and to inform Parliament of the causes of its summons. Provision is made for discussion of matters referred to in such address.
content.glance: Special address to both Houses: first session after each LS general election, and first session of each year. Causes of summons; discussion follows.
content.study:
Article 87:
(1) At the commencement of the first session after each general election to the House of the People and at the commencement of the first session of each year the President shall address both Houses of Parliament assembled together and inform Parliament of the causes of its summons.
(2) Provision shall be made by the rules regulating the procedure of either House for the allotment of time for discussion of the matters referred to in such address.

Examination: two occasions for special address; both Houses assembled together; causes of summons; rules provide time for discussion.

sections.heading: Occasions
sections.body:
1. Commencement of the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha.
2. Commencement of the first session of each year.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When does the President give a special address under Article 87?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 87, the President addresses both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election to the House of the People and at the commencement of the first session of each year, and informs Parliament of the causes of its summons. Rules provide time for discussion of the matters referred to in the address.

examTips: Two occasions: post-LS election first session; first session of each year.

keyTakeaways: Art 87: special address post-LS election and first session of each year.
